red_team.case_for_morning: The NROL-136 listings were still 'Go, 21 Nov 12:30Z, SLC-4E, no slips' (Orbital Radar, modified 20 Nov). The best path for the morning figure: SpaceX puts the NRO mission first. If USSF-317 stands down again or is moved behind NROL-136 (customer priority, or more trouble after Thursday's unexplained scrub), NROL-136 keeps its Sat 04:30 PST slot. Smaller paths: a pad listing is wrong, or the pad is recycled in a record ~10 h. None of these is reported; no source puts NROL-136 on SLC-6.
red_team.case_for_larger: NROL-136 has one 30-minute attempt in the window and no next-day margin. A ~10 h same-pad recycle has never been done at SLC-4E. If USSF-317 scrubs again its next slot (Sat 18:32 PST) still blocks the pad. Weather (49% rain forecast for USSF-317) adds risk. A fair figure could be 2–3%.
red_team.verdict: The revision is right; the case for the morning figure is much weaker and rests on an unreported reorder or a stale pad listing, both weighed by the forecasters. It is a timing fact (p_held). 5%, the calibrated figure, is published; 3–5% would be defensible.
